answer: Sybil resistance follows because identity verification requires a continuous chain of sequential modular squarings, as in a Wesolowski VDF, where each result determines the next input. An attacker may imitate many identities, but GPUs cannot parallelize the dependencies within each chain or reduce its enforced delay; clones therefore consume proportional hardware and elapsed time. A nebula, ripple, or island of machines gains throughput only by duplicating costly sequential executions.
